question.prompt:
Three members of the Euclid Middle School girls’ softball team had the following conversation.

Ashley: I just realized that our uniform numbers are all \(2\)-digit primes.

Bethany: And the sum of your two uniform numbers is the date of my birthday earlier this month.

Caitlin: That’s funny. The sum of your two uniform numbers is the date of my birthday later this month.

Ashley: And the sum of your two uniform numbers is today’s date.

What number does Caitlin wear?

solutions.explanation:
The birthdays are on opposite sides of today, so their order lets us compare the uniform numbers. Let Ashley's, Bethany's, and Caitlin's numbers be \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), respectively. Bethany's birthday, today, and Caitlin's birthday have dates \(a+c\), \(b+c\), and \(a+b\). Therefore
\[
a+c<b+c<a+b.
\]
Comparing the first two sums gives \(a<b\), and comparing the last two gives \(c<a\). Thus \(c<a<b\), so the numbers are distinct.

The smallest two-digit primes are \(11\), \(13\), and \(17\). Consequently, \(a\geq13\) and \(b\geq17\). Caitlin's birthday date is \(a+b\), and no month has more than \(31\) days. Hence
\[
a\leq31-17=14.
\]
The only prime from \(13\) through \(14\) is \(13\), so \(a=13\). Now \(13<b\leq18\), which forces \(b=17\). The only two-digit prime smaller than \(13\) is \(11\), so \(c=11\).

These numbers give Bethany's birthday as the \(24\)th, today as the \(28\)th, and Caitlin's birthday as the \(30\)th, which is possible in a month with at least \(30\) days. Caitlin wears \(\boxed{11}\), choice A.
solutions.title: Compare the birthday dates
